name: Ears & your own voice

overlay.caption: your voice reaches your ears through the air AND through your skull; a recording catches only the air

does: Shows your own voice reaching your ears through bone as well as through the air
Shows the bone route adding mostly low, deep sound
Shows plugging your ears making the bone route louder
doesnt: Measure any real person or any real microphone
Include hearing loss or how the brain processes voices
Say how anyone's voice should sound
limits.text: This is a simplified learning model. Real people vary with age, fitness and health. The numbers are illustrative, not measurements of any real person.
limits.wellbeing: If your own voice suddenly sounds very loud or echoey to you and it doesn't go away, tell an adult.

sources: NIH NIDCD: how do we hear? (student pages)
